title: Yet the Spirit is given unequally: spiritual and carnal believers in 1 Corinthians 3
pass_a_gloss: But that Spirit is given unequally, and not to all by the same measure. Hence it is that, although each and every believer has God's Spirit, at least in some degree, some of them are nonetheless called spiritual, over against others who are called carnal, as may be seen in 1 Corinthians 3. And I, brothers, says Paul, could not speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to carnal: as to infants in Christ. For Paul does not call them brothers unless they are believers. And yet those he addresses there he says are carnal — that is, still crude and weak in mind, who have not yet received the Spirit of Christ in that measure by which they can bear and grasp the more hidden and difficult mysteries of the Christian religion: and therefore, as he himself says, they are as it were infants in Christ. By the spiritual, however, he understands those whom the Holy Spirit has raised into a more perfect state.
pass_b_english: Yet that Spirit is given unequally, not to all by the same measure. So although every believer has God’s Spirit at least in some degree, some are still called spiritual over against others called carnal, as in 1 Corinthians 3.

Paul says: "And I, brothers, could not speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to carnal: as to infants in Christ." He does not call them brothers unless they are believers. Yet those he addresses there he calls carnal — still crude and weak in mind, who have not yet received Christ’s Spirit in the measure needed to bear and grasp the more hidden, harder mysteries of the Christian religion. So, as he says, they are as it were infants in Christ. By "the spiritual" he means those the Holy Spirit has raised into a more perfect state.
source_text: XII. Verum Spiritus ille inaequaliter datur, nec omnibus eadem mensura. Unde est quod, tametsi omnes et singuli fideles Spiritum Dei habent, aliquo saltem gradu, quidam tamen eorum spirituales vocantur, opposite ad alios, qui dicuntur carnales, ut videre est, 1. Cor. 3. Et Ego fratres, inquit Paulus, non potui loqui vobis quasi spiritualibus, sed quasi carnalibus: tanquam parvulis in Christo. Nam fratres suos Paulus non vocat, nisi fideles. Et tamen quos ibi compellat, dicit esse carnales, id est, rudes adhuc et mente imbecilla, quique ea mensura Spiritum Christi adhuc non acceperunt, ut ferre et capere possint religionis Christianae mysteria magis abstrusa atque difficilia: ideoque, ut ipse dicit, in Christo quasi infantes. Per spirituales autem intelligit illos quos Spiritus sanctus in statum perfectiorem evexit.
